A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. All 13 pages of each version, including Appendix A, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on layer selection, training-data size, computational cost, language retention, and pruning.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations and validation using Bunny-Phi3-mini-4B-V.

M1.justification: Sparse and uniform layer tuning, the selected layer indices, and angular-distance pruning outside the visual region remain unchanged. The Phi-3 validation applies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMMU and SEED-IMG to the visual evaluations and C-Eval and CMMLU to the textual evaluations. These additions substantially broaden multimodal reasoning coverage and extend language-retention evaluation to Chinese. Existing datasets remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same heuristic and importance-based comparison methods. The full-training, selective-training, and language-backbone comparisons also remain. Phi-3 extends model validation using the existing comparison design.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 32-layer Phi-3-mini-4B testbed comparing full-layer and eight-layer tuning, and specifies five-shot evaluation for C-Eval and CMMLU. Visual averages now cover ten benchmarks rather than eight; retained experimental settings are otherwise unchanged.

E4.justification: The Section 4.2 footnote newly reports that odd-numbered layer selections perform slightly worse and that alternative one- and two-layer configurations were tested. The existing data-size sensitivity and pruning analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and relative-performance percentages without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional results retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 add substantial results for the four new benchmarks and Phi-3 validation. For example, Table 3 reports Phi-3 averages of 60.16% for eight-layer tuning versus 61.17% for full tuning. Existing per-task scores are retained; revised visual averages reflect expanded benchmark coverage, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same definitions and formulas for block influence, multimodal block influence, parameter change, angular distance, and image attention. No new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that tuning roughly 25% of sparsely distributed layers preserves nearly 99% of visual performance, better preserves textual abilities, reduces training cost, and supports visual-region-based pruning. Expanded validation supports these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly emphasizes that importance-based selection requires a fully trained model, while heuristic selection avoids that prerequisite. v2 also predicts greater relative computational savings at larger scales and characterizes pruning as an initial exploration.

D1.justification: v2 removes the DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 and 8×A800 training specification from Section 3.1 and the identification of LLaVA evaluation code from Section 3.2. A800 hardware remains mentioned in Section 5.2. These are documentation removals, not established changes to the experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Phi-3, MMMU, SEED-Bench, C-Eval, and CMMLU, and removes the COCO and DeepSpeed4Science references. Section 4.1 expands positioning against post-hoc importance selection; the dedicated related-work section is essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and several explanatory paragraphs are condensed or rewritten, evaluation-task subsections become inline numbered descriptions, and author affiliations are updated. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–4 gain benchmark columns, Table 3 gains Phi-3 rows, and table formatting becomes denser. Figure 3 moves and Figure 1's caption expands. All five figure graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Chinese-language evaluations and Phi-3 validation strengthen evidence for the existing generalizability and language-retention claims, while Section 4.1 clarifies selection costs. The net gain is limited by removed reproducibility details and a new inconsistency: the identical eight-layer results have averages of 61.82% in Table 1 and 61.78% in Table 2.
